researchSources.authority: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration
researchSources.title: Powered Industrial Trucks — Narrow Aisles
researchSources.designUse: conventional counterbalanced-truck rack aisles use approximately 12 feet; narrower aisles require specialized trucks

researchSources.authority: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration
researchSources.title: Powered Industrial Trucks — Enclosed and Hazardous Areas
researchSources.designUse: enclosed vehicle areas require adequate ventilation and carbon-monoxide controls; the underground vehicle hall receives dedicated mechanical exhaust and monitoring

researchSources.authority: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration
researchSources.title: 1910.36 Design and construction requirements for exit routes
researchSources.designUse: at least two remote exits, permanent fire-separated exits, direct discharge, outward swing for higher occupant loads, minimum headroom and clear width

researchSources.authority: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration
researchSources.title: 1910.141 Sanitation
researchSources.designUse: dry sanitary workrooms, potable water, private toilet compartments, waste and vermin control

researchSources.title: 2010 ADA Standards — Chapter 4 Accessible Routes
researchSources.designUse: pedestrian ramp maximum 1:12, level landings, stable surfaces, edge protection, accessible route independent of vehicle ramp

researchSources.title: Truck Parking Development Handbook
researchSources.designUse: WB-67 swept-path method, 53-foot trailer and 8.5-foot width reference, access/circulation/parking geometry

researchSources.title: Federal Lands Highway Design, Chapter 9
researchSources.designUse: select a design vehicle and test inside radii and encroachment rather than guessing at corner geometry

researchSources.title: Standards and Regulations
researchSources.designUse: walk-in display units remain temporary-living-quarter vehicles; safety, electrical, plumbing, heating and fire-life-safety systems must read as complete

researchSources.title: NFPA 30A extracts in NFPA 1 proposed text
researchSources.designUse: motor-fuel dispensing and repair areas are distinct special-purpose hazards with drainage, egress and suppression requirements

researchSources.title: Release Prevention for Underground Storage Tanks
researchSources.designUse: travel-center fuel area requires spill/overfill prevention and a mapped tank/transfer system; represented symbolically only in Minecraft

researchSources.title: 2022 Food Code
researchSources.designUse: commercial kitchens receive controlled food, warewashing, handwashing, waste and service paths isolated from repair, fuel and private-wellness zones

researchSources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
researchSources.title: Key Findings and Recommendations — The Station Nightclub Fire
researchSources.designUse: nightclub uses sprinklers, remote redundant exits, distributed egress capacity, low-level wayfinding and no pyrotechnics or ignitable foam

researchSources.authority: U.S. Department of Defense Whole Building Design Guide
researchSources.title: Supply and Administration Warehouse Design Guide
researchSources.designUse: organize receiving, distribution, counter service, administration, open warehouse and loading functions as a legible operational sequence
